newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel declines against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel declines against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel representative rate was fixed lower against the dollar on Tuesday following the rise of the U.S. currency on overseas markets, dealers said.
"The rise of the dollar in Europe pushed the basket downward and the Bank of Israel had to intervene again in the market buying dollars," said a dealer at Bank Hapoalim.
"Overall volume was low and the Bank of Israel bought dollars on a relatively small scale," he said.
Traders estimated that the central bank bought about $50 million.

The shekel is allowed to fluctuate in a trading band of seven percent above or below a sloping mid-point designed to devalue the Israeli currency at a rate of six percent a year against the basket of key currencies.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3590 shekels against 3.3510 on Monday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6378 shekels against 3.6368 on Monday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7042 shekels per 100 yen against 2.6983 on Monday and against the mark at 1.9734 shekels against 1.9776 on Monday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.3580 shekels.
